source.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּשִּׁטִּ֑ים וַיָּ֣חֶל הָעָ֔ם לִזְנ֖וֹת אֶל־בְּנ֥וֹת מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And stayed Israel in Shittim, and began the people to prostitute [themselves] with [the] daughters of Moab.

en.L: And Israel stayed in Shittim, and the people began to prostitute themselves with the daughters of Moab.
en.B: Israel settled at Shittim, and there the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab.
en.R: Israel was camped at a place called Shittim. There the men began to have sex with Moabite women.

es.L: Y se quedó Israel en Sitim, y comenzó el pueblo a prostituirse con las hijas de Moab.
es.B: Israel se estableció en Sitim, y allí el pueblo empezó a tener relaciones sexuales inmorales con las mujeres de Moab.
es.R: Israel estaba acampado en un lugar llamado Sitim. Allí los hombres comenzaron a acostarse con mujeres moabitas.

fr.L: Et Israël demeura à Shittim, et le peuple commença à se prostituer avec les filles de Moab.
fr.B: Israël s’établit à Shittim, et là le peuple commença à se livrer à la débauche avec les femmes de Moab.
fr.R: Israël campait dans un lieu appelé Shittim. Là, les hommes ont commencé à coucher avec des femmes moabites.

sw.L: Naye Israeli akakaa Shitimu, na watu wakaanza kufanya ukahaba pamoja na binti za Moabu.
sw.B: Israeli alipokuwa akikaa Shitimu, watu walianza kufanya uasherati na wanawake wa Moabu.
sw.R: Waisraeli walikuwa wamepiga kambi mahali panapoitwa Shitimu. Huko wanaume walianza kulala na wanawake wa Kimoabu.

decisions.choice: Shittim: Israel's last camp east of the Jordan, in the plains of Moab
decisions.reason: Israel had camped in the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho (22:1). Shittim, called Abel-shittim in 33:49, is the place from which Joshua later sends the spies and the people set out to cross the river (Joshua 2:1; 3:1). The name means "acacia trees".

decisions.choice: prostitute themselves: sexual relations outside marriage that lead into the worship of other gods
alternatives: be unfaithful to God only, without sexual sin
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a woman who sells herself or is unfaithful, and often of Israel turning to other gods (Exodus 34:15-16; Judges 2:17). Here both senses meet: the men had sexual relations with Moabite women, and verses 2-3 show where it led. The word does not say that the women were paid.

decisions.choice: the danger the covenant warned of in Exodus 34:15-16
decisions.reason: The LORD had warned that if Israel made ties with the peoples of the land, they would be invited to the sacrifices of their gods and eat, and their daughters would lead Israel's sons to prostitute themselves to their gods (Exodus 34:15-16). Verses 1-2 tell that warning coming true, in the same words. Numbers 31:16 adds that the scheme came from Balaam's advice.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the people", but the partners named are women, and the people meant are the men of Israel. Readable says so; Literal and Balanced keep "the people". Readable also says "have sex" for the verb, keeping the sexual sense plain; the turn to other gods follows in the next verse.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("demeura", "commença"); passé composé at Readable ("ont commencé")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken and school French.

source.text: וַתִּקְרֶ֣אןָ לָעָ֔ם לְזִבְחֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אכַל הָעָ֔ם וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֖וּלֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they invited the people to [the] sacrifices of their gods, and ate the people and bowed down to their gods.

en.L: And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
en.B: These women invited the people to the sacrifices for their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
en.R: The women invited them to the feasts where they offered sacrifices to their gods. The people ate the meat of the sacrifices and bowed down to worship those gods.

es.L: Y ellas invitaron al pueblo a los sacrificios de sus dioses, y comió el pueblo y se postró ante sus dioses.
es.B: Estas mujeres invitaron al pueblo a los sacrificios en honor de sus dioses, y el pueblo comió y se inclinó ante sus dioses.
es.R: Las mujeres los invitaron a las fiestas en que ofrecían sacrificios a sus dioses. El pueblo comió la carne de los sacrificios y se inclinó para adorar a esos dioses.

fr.L: Et elles invitèrent le peuple aux sacrifices de leurs dieux, et le peuple mangea et se prosterna devant leurs dieux.
fr.B: Ces femmes invitèrent le peuple aux sacrifices offerts à leurs dieux, et le peuple mangea et se prosterna devant leurs dieux.
fr.R: Les femmes les ont invités aux fêtes où elles offraient des sacrifices à leurs dieux. Le peuple a mangé la viande des sacrifices et s’est prosterné pour adorer ces dieux.

sw.L: Nao wakawaalika watu kwenye dhabihu za miungu yao, nao watu wakala, wakasujudu mbele ya miungu yao.
sw.B: Wanawake hao waliwaalika watu kwenye dhabihu zilizotolewa kwa miungu yao, nao watu wakala na kusujudu mbele ya miungu yao.
sw.R: Wanawake hao waliwaalika kwenye karamu ambapo walitoa dhabihu kwa miungu yao. Watu wakala nyama ya dhabihu, wakainama kuiabudu miungu hiyo.

decisions.choice: they ... their gods: the Moabite women and their gods
decisions.reason: The verb "invited" and both words for "their" are feminine plural, so they point back to the daughters of Moab in verse 1. The gods are the women's gods, not Israel's.

decisions.choice: the sacrifices ... ate: a sacrificial meal in honor of the gods
decisions.reason: Many sacrifices ended in a feast where the worshipers ate part of the animal (as in the peace offering, Leviticus 7:15). To eat such a meal was to share in the worship of the god it was offered to (Exodus 34:15; compare 1 Corinthians 10:18-21). Psalm 106:28 recalls this meal.

decisions.choice: These women / The women
decisions.reason: English "they" does not show that the subject is feminine, so Balanced and Readable name the women. Readable also adds "the meat of the sacrifices" and "to worship" to make the meal and the bowing plain (m2).

decisions.choice: "elles invitèrent"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is feminine plural, pointing to the daughters of Moab (m2). French can show this with "elles", so Literal keeps the pronoun without naming the women, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וַיִּצָּ֥מֶד יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And yoked itself Israel to Baal of Peor, and burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel.

en.L: And Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel.
en.B: So Israel bound itself to the Baal of Peor, and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel.
en.R: So Israel joined in worshiping Baal, the god of Peor. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with Israel.

es.L: Y se unció Israel a Baal de Peor, y se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra Israel.
es.B: Así Israel se ató al Baal de Peor, y la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} ardió contra Israel.
es.R: Así Israel se unió a la adoración de Baal, el dios de Peor. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con Israel.

fr.L: Et Israël s’attela à Baal de Peor, et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël.
fr.B: Israël se lia ainsi au Baal de Peor, et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël.
fr.R: Ainsi Israël s’est joint au culte de Baal, le dieu de Peor. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est mis très en colère contre Israël.

sw.L: Naye Israeli akajifunga nira pamoja na Baali wa Peori, nayo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka juu ya Israeli.
sw.B: Hivyo Israeli akajifunga kwa Baali wa Peori, nayo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka dhidi ya Israeli.
sw.R: Hivyo Waisraeli walijiunga katika kumwabudu Baali, mungu wa Peori. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawakasirikia Waisraeli sana.

decisions.choice: yoked itself: bound itself in worship, like an animal joined to a yoke
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a pair or yoke of animals (1 Samuel 11:7). Israel tied itself to Baal of Peor as its god, the bond it owed to the LORD alone. Psalm 106:28 and verse 5 use the same verb.

decisions.choice: Baal of Peor: the Baal worshiped at Peor
decisions.reason: Baal ("lord, master") was the name of a Canaanite storm god and was used for local gods in many places. Peor was a mountain in Moab where Balak had taken Balaam (23:28); Beth-peor nearby was a town of the region (Deuteronomy 3:29). Baal of Peor is the god as worshiped there. The event is remembered in Deuteronomy 4:3, Hosea 9:10 and Psalm 106:28.

decisions.choice: joined in worshiping
decisions.reason: Readable states the meaning of the picture (m1) instead of keeping it, and the idiom "anger burned" becomes "became very angry".

decisions.choice: "se unció" (yoked itself)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of an animal put under a yoke (m1); "uncirse" is the Spanish verb for that. Balanced says "se ató" (bound itself).

decisions.choice: "s'attela" (harnessed itself)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a draught animal put to the yoke (m1); "s'atteler" is the French verb for harnessing. Balanced says "se lia" (bound itself).

decisions.choice: "akajifunga nira" (put on himself a yoke)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the yoke (m1) by naming it, "nira"; Balanced says only "akajifunga" (bound himself).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה קַ֚ח אֶת־כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְהוֹקַ֥ע אוֹתָ֛ם לַיהוָ֖ה נֶ֣גֶד הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְיָשֹׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף־יְהוָ֖ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, take all [the] heads of the people and impale them to Yahweh before the sun, so that may turn [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh from Israel.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take all the heads of the people and impale them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} before the sun, so that the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may turn from Israel."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and impale them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the light of day, so that the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will leave Israel."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Gather all the leaders of the people and put them to death. Then hang their bodies on poles in the open daylight, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When that is done, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will no longer be so fiercely angry with Israel."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «Toma a todos los cabezas del pueblo y empálalos para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} frente al sol, para que se aparte de Israel el ardor de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.»
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Toma a todos los jefes del pueblo y empálalos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a plena luz del día, para que la ardiente ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se aparte de Israel.»
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Reúne a todos los jefes del pueblo y hazlos morir. Luego cuelga sus cuerpos en postes a la luz del día, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Cuando eso esté hecho, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ya no estará tan furioso con Israel.»

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Prends tous les chefs du peuple et empale-les pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} face au soleil, afin que l’ardeur de la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} se détourne d’Israël. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Prends tous les chefs du peuple et empale-les devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en plein jour, pour que l’ardente colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} se retire d’Israël. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Rassemble tous les chefs du peuple et fais-les mourir. Ensuite, suspends leurs corps à des poteaux, en plein jour, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Quand ce sera fait, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne sera plus aussi furieux contre Israël. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Uwachukue wakuu wote wa watu, ukawatundike juu ya nguzo kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mbele ya jua, ili ukali wa hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ugeuke uondoke kwa Israeli."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Wachukue viongozi wote wa watu, uwatundike juu ya nguzo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mchana kweupe, ili hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iondoke kwa Israeli."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Wakusanye viongozi wote wa watu, uwaue. Kisha itundike miili yao juu ya nguzo mchana kweupe, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hilo likishafanyika, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hatakuwa tena na hasira kali hivyo dhidi ya Israeli."

decisions.choice: impale: put to death and display the bodies on stakes
decisions.reason: This form of the verb occurs only here and in 2 Samuel 21:6, 9, 13, where seven of Saul's descendants are put to death and their bodies left exposed "before the LORD". A related form means to be put out of joint (Genesis 32:26). The exact method is not certain: impaling, hanging, or breaking the limbs have all been suggested. What is clear is a public execution with the bodies left on display.

decisions.choice: them: the heads of the people
alternatives: the guilty men, whom the leaders are to seize and put to death
decisions.reason: In the grammar, "them" most naturally refers to the heads of the people, who are held responsible for the people they lead. But in the next verse Moses tells the judges to kill only those who had joined themselves to Baal of Peor, so "them" may mean the guilty, with the leaders as the ones who carry out the sentence. The text keeps "them" and leaves this open.

decisions.choice: before the sun: openly, in daylight
decisions.reason: The phrase means in full view, in broad daylight (2 Samuel 12:11-12). The punishment is to be public, before the LORD and before all Israel.

decisions.choice: put them to death. Then hang their bodies on poles
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the death and the display that the one verb implies (m1). Balanced and Readable say "before" the LORD for "to" the LORD: the act is done in his presence and for him.

decisions.choice: "ukawatundike juu ya nguzo" (hang them on poles)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday verb for impaling. "Kuwatundika juu ya nguzo" names the public display of the bodies (m1) without the Christian associations of "kusulubisha" (to crucify).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶל־שֹׁפְטֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִרְגוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֲנָשָׁ֔יו הַנִּצְמָדִ֖ים לְבַ֥עַל פְּעֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to [the] judges of Israel, kill each his men who yoked themselves to Baal of Peor.

en.L: And Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Kill, each [of you], his men who yoked themselves to Baal of Peor."
en.B: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you is to kill the men under his authority who have bound themselves to the Baal of Peor."
en.R: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Every one of you is to put to death the men under you who joined in worshiping Baal, the god of Peor."

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a los jueces de Israel: «{{plural_you:Maten|Matad}}, cada uno [de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}], a sus hombres que se uncieron a Baal de Peor.»
es.B: Entonces Moisés dijo a los jueces de Israel: «Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe matar a los hombres que están bajo su autoridad y que se han atado al Baal de Peor.»
es.R: Entonces Moisés dijo a los jueces de Israel: «Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tiene que dar muerte a los hombres a su cargo que se unieron a la adoración de Baal, el dios de Peor.»

fr.L: Et Moïse dit aux juges d’Israël : « Tuez, chacun [de vous], ses hommes qui se sont attelés à Baal de Peor. »
fr.B: Moïse dit donc aux juges d’Israël : « Que chacun de vous tue les hommes placés sous son autorité qui se sont liés au Baal de Peor. »
fr.R: Alors Moïse a dit aux juges d’Israël : « Chacun de vous doit faire mourir les hommes dont il a la charge et qui se sont joints au culte de Baal, le dieu de Peor. »

sw.L: Naye Musa akawaambia waamuzi wa Israeli, "Waueni, kila mmoja [wenu], watu wake waliojifunga nira pamoja na Baali wa Peori."
sw.B: Basi Musa akawaambia waamuzi wa Israeli, "Kila mmoja wenu na awaue watu walio chini ya mamlaka yake waliojifunga kwa Baali wa Peori."
sw.R: Basi Musa akawaambia waamuzi wa Israeli, "Kila mmoja wenu lazima awaue watu walio chini yake walioshiriki kumwabudu Baali, mungu wa Peori."

decisions.choice: the judges ... his men: each judge over the men under his authority
decisions.reason: Since the time of Exodus 18:21-26, judges had been set over groups of the people to settle their cases. "His men" are those each judge is responsible for. The guilt is limited to those who had bound themselves to Baal of Peor (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Moses' order: the account does not say it was carried out
decisions.reason: The story turns at once to the man who brings a Midianite woman into the camp (verse 6). How Moses' order relates to the LORD's command in verse 4, and whether the judges acted, is not told.

decisions.choice: Each of you is to kill the men under his authority / Every one of you is to put to death the men under you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "kill, each his men" is a command to the judges one by one. Literal brackets "of you"; Balanced and Readable make it a full English sentence.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֡ה אִישׁ֩ מִבְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בָּ֗א וַיַּקְרֵ֤ב אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִ֔ית לְעֵינֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֣מָּה בֹכִ֔ים פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, a man from [the] sons of Israel came and brought near to his brothers the Midianite [woman] in [the] eyes of Moses and in [the] eyes of all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, and they [were] weeping [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And look, a man from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel came and brought near to his brothers the Midianite [woman] in the eyes of Moses and in the eyes of all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, while they [were] weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: Just then one of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came and brought a Midianite woman to his relatives. He did it in full view of Moses and the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as they wept at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Just then an Israelite man came and brought a Midianite woman to his family. He did it while Moses and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were watching. They were weeping at the entrance of the meeting tent.

es.L: Y he aquí, un hombre de los hijos de Israel vino y trajo a sus hermanos a la madianita, a los ojos de Moisés y a los ojos de toda la comunidad de los hijos de Israel, mientras ellos [estaban] llorando a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.B: En ese momento llegó uno de los israelitas y llevó a una mujer madianita a donde estaban sus parientes. Lo hizo a la vista de Moisés y de toda la comunidad de los israelitas, mientras lloraban a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.R: En ese momento, un israelita llegó con una mujer madianita y la llevó a su familia. Lo hizo mientras Moisés y todos los israelitas estaban mirando. Ellos lloraban a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.

fr.L: Et voici, un homme d’entre les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël vint et amena à ses frères la Madianite, aux yeux de Moïse et aux yeux de toute la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, tandis qu’ils [étaient] en pleurs à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.B: Juste à ce moment, un des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} arriva et amena une Madianite auprès des siens. Il le fit sous les yeux de Moïse et de toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, alors qu’ils pleuraient à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, un Israélite est arrivé avec une Madianite et l’a amenée dans sa famille. Il l’a fait pendant que Moïse et tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} regardaient. Ils pleuraient à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.

sw.L: Na tazama, mtu mmoja wa wana wa Israeli akaja, akamleta kwa ndugu zake yule [mwanamke] Mmidiani, machoni pa Musa na machoni pa jumuiya yote ya wana wa Israeli, nao [walikuwa] wakilia mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.B: Wakati huo huo, mmoja wa Waisraeli alikuja akamleta mwanamke Mmidiani kwa jamaa zake. Alifanya hivyo mbele ya macho ya Musa na ya jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli, walipokuwa wakilia kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo Mwisraeli mmoja alikuja akamleta mwanamke Mmidiani kwa familia yake. Alifanya hivyo Musa na Waisraeli wote wakiwa wanaangalia. Walikuwa wakilia kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.

decisions.choice: brought near to his brothers: brought her among his own relatives in the camp
alternatives: brought her near to his fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "His brothers" here means his kin, the people of his family and clan (verse 14 names his family among the Simeonites). He brought her openly into the camp, among his own people. The text does not say whether this was a marriage or a visit to a shrine (see verse 8).

decisions.choice: the Midianite woman: a particular woman, named in verse 15
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the Midianite", feminine, pointing to the woman the story is about. The Midianites had joined Moab's leaders against Israel (22:4, 7), and verses 17-18 hold them responsible for the whole affair.

decisions.choice: weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting: mourning and pleading before the LORD
decisions.reason: The people who wept were gathered where Israel met the LORD, grieving over the sin and its punishment; the plague of verses 8-9 was already striking. The man's act in front of them all is open defiance.

decisions.choice: Just then ... in full view of / while ... were watching
decisions.reason: "Look" calls attention to a sudden event; Balanced and Readable say "Just then". "In the eyes of" means in full view; Readable says they were watching. Balanced and Readable say "relatives" and "family" for "his brothers" (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֗רְא פִּֽינְחָס֙ בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַיָּ֨קָם֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֥ח רֹ֖מַח בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, and he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.

en.L: And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw [it], and he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
en.B: When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he stood up from among the congregation and seized a spear.
en.R: Phinehas saw it. He was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron the priest. He got up and left the people, and he took a spear in his hand.

fr.L: Et Phinéas, fils d’Éléazar, fils d’Aaron le prêtre, [le] vit, et il se leva du milieu de la communauté et prit une lance dans sa main.
fr.B: Quand Phinéas, fils d’Éléazar, fils du prêtre Aaron, vit cela, il se leva du milieu de la communauté et saisit une lance.

sw.L: Naye Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari, mwana wa Haruni kuhani, akaona [hilo], akainuka kutoka katikati ya jumuiya, akatwaa mkuki mkononi mwake.

decisions.choice: Phinehas: grandson of Aaron, son of the high priest Eleazar
decisions.reason: Aaron had died and his son Eleazar now served as high priest (20:25-28). Phinehas, Eleazar's son (Exodus 6:25), later goes to war as priest (31:6) and serves at the ark (Judges 20:28). "The priest" can describe Aaron, whose name stands next to it, or Phinehas himself, as in verse 11; either way Phinehas belonged to the priestly line.

decisions.choice: He was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron
alternatives: son of Eleazar son of Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable puts the family line in a sentence of its own and says "grandson" for the second "son of".

fr.B: Il suivit l’Israélite dans l’alcôve de la tente et les transperça de sa lance tous les deux, l’Israélite et la femme, à travers le ventre de celle-ci. Et le fléau qui frappait les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} s’arrêta.

sw.L: Naye akamfuata yule mtu wa Israeli mpaka ndani ya hema la ndani, akawachoma wote wawili, yule mtu wa Israeli na yule mwanamke, tumboni mwake; nalo pigo likazuiliwa juu ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Alimfuata yule Mwisraeli hadi katika chumba cha ndani cha hema, akawachoma mkuki wote wawili, yule Mwisraeli na yule mwanamke, kupitia tumbo la mwanamke. Nalo pigo lililokuwa likiwapiga Waisraeli likakoma.
sw.R: Alimfuata yule Mwisraeli hadi chumba cha ndani cha hema. Akaupitisha mkuki wake katika mwili wa yule mtu mpaka tumboni mwa yule mwanamke, akawaua wote wawili. Kisha ugonjwa wa kuua uliokuwa umewapata Waisraeli ukakoma.

decisions.choice: the tent-chamber: an inner room or alcove of a tent
decisions.reason: This word occurs only here in the Bible. It seems to be a vaulted inner room or alcove of a tent, perhaps a sleeping room. Some have suggested a tent used for worship, where the two were taking part in a rite, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: her belly: her stomach or lower body
decisions.reason: The word for her body sounds like the word for the tent-chamber earlier in the verse, a play on words in the Hebrew. It most likely means her belly; it may also point to the sexual act the two were engaged in.

decisions.choice: the plague: a deadly sickness sent by the LORD in his anger
decisions.reason: The plague has not been mentioned before; it is the LORD's anger of verses 3-4 at work, as in 17:11-15 and 14:37. Phinehas' act turned the anger away and the plague stopped (verse 11; Psalm 106:29-30).

decisions.choice: ran the spear through / thrust his spear through
decisions.reason: The verb means to pierce or run through. Balanced and Readable name the spear of verse 7. Readable says "deadly sickness" for "plague", a word young readers may not know.

decisions.choice: "l'alcôve de la tente"
decisions.reason: The rare word seems to name a vaulted inner room or recess of a tent (m1); "alcôve" is the French word for such a recess. Literal keeps "la tente intérieure" as the English Literal does; Readable says "la pièce du fond".

Numbers above ninety-nine are written in figures (style guide). Readable says "from it" for "in the plague", which it has just named.

source.text: פִּֽינְחָ֨ס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֜ר בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־חֲמָתִי֙ מֵעַ֣ל בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּקַנְא֥וֹ אֶת־קִנְאָתִ֖י בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְלֹא־כִלִּ֥יתִי אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּקִנְאָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest has turned back my wrath from on [the] sons of Israel in his being jealous [with] my jealousy in their midst, and not I made an end of [the] sons of Israel in my jealousy.

en.L: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, in that he was jealous with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy in their midst, and I did not put an end to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy.
en.B: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath away from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, because he burned with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} zeal among them. So I did not wipe out the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} zeal.
en.R: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, the grandson of Aaron the priest, has stopped {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He shared {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burning zeal and acted on it among them. Because of that, I did not wipe out the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} zeal.

es.L: «Finés hijo de Eleazar, hijo de Aarón el sacerdote, ha hecho volver {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor de sobre los hijos de Israel, en cuanto fue celoso con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo en medio de ellos, y no acabé con los hijos de Israel en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo.
es.B: «Finés hijo de Eleazar, hijo del sacerdote Aarón, ha apartado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor de los israelitas, porque ardió con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo entre ellos. Por eso no exterminé a los israelitas en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo.
es.R: «Finés hijo de Eleazar, nieto del sacerdote Aarón, ha detenido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo contra los israelitas. Él compartió {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo ardiente y actuó conforme a él entre ellos. Por eso no destruí a los israelitas en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} celo.

fr.L: « Phinéas, fils d’Éléazar, fils d’Aaron le prêtre, a détourné {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur de dessus les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, en ce qu’il a été jaloux de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} jalousie au milieu d’eux, et je n’ai pas mis fin aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} jalousie.
fr.B: « Phinéas, fils d’Éléazar, fils du prêtre Aaron, a détourné {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, parce qu’il a brûlé de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} zèle parmi eux. C’est pourquoi je n’ai pas anéanti les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} zèle.
fr.R: « Phinéas, fils d’Éléazar et petit-fils du prêtre Aaron, a arrêté {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère contre les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Il a partagé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} zèle brûlant et il a agi selon ce zèle au milieu d’eux. C’est pour cela que je n’ai pas fait disparaître les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} zèle.

sw.L: "Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari, mwana wa Haruni kuhani, ameigeuza ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iondoke juu ya wana wa Israeli, kwa kuwa alikuwa na wivu kwa wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katikati yao, wala sikuwamaliza wana wa Israeli katika wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.B: "Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari, mwana wa kuhani Haruni, ameiondoa ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa Waisraeli, kwa sababu aliwaka wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kati yao. Kwa hiyo sikuwaangamiza Waisraeli katika wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.R: "Finehasi mwana wa Eleazari, mjukuu wa kuhani Haruni, ameizuia hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} dhidi ya Waisraeli. Alishiriki wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mkali, akatenda kwa wivu huo katikati yao. Kwa sababu hiyo sikuwaangamiza Waisraeli katika wivu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

decisions.choice: jealous with my jealousy: a burning zeal for God's honor and his exclusive claim on Israel
decisions.reason: The word describes intense, protective passion. Used of God it is his refusal to share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14, where the LORD's name is "Jealous"). Phinehas felt the same passion God felt at Israel's betrayal and acted on it. It is not envy. The same word in "my jealousy" at the end of the verse is the passion that would have destroyed Israel.

decisions.choice: has turned back my wrath: his act ended the punishment
decisions.reason: The LORD's anger had been burning against Israel and the plague was killing the people (verses 3, 8-9). By dealing with the open sin in their midst, Phinehas stood between the people and that anger, as Aaron had done with incense in 17:11-13 and as Psalm 106:30 remembers. Verse 13 calls this making atonement.

decisions.choice: zeal
decisions.reason: In English, "jealous" usually suggests envy or suspicion, which is not the sense here (m1). Literal keeps "jealous ... jealousy" to show the repeated word; Balanced and Readable say "zeal" and keep it the same each time. Readable says "anger" for "wrath".

decisions.choice: "il a été jaloux de ma jalousie"
alternatives: "il a été animé de mon zèle"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb and noun of one root, as the English Literal does. Here "de" means "with" (filled with my jealousy), not "envious of". Balanced and Readable say "zèle", as the English says "zeal".

decisions.choice: "wivu" at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced and Readable say "zeal", Swahili keeps "wivu": used of God it is the protective passion of "Mungu mwenye wivu" (Exodus 20:5), not envy, and it keeps the link with that phrase. "Bidii" and "ari" would say only effort or eagerness.

en.R: So announce this: 'I am giving him {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant of peace.

decisions.choice: my covenant of peace: a covenant that sets him in lasting peace and well-being with God
decisions.reason: "Peace" here is wholeness and safety in a right relationship, given by God. The covenant is the LORD's own ("my covenant"), freely granted. Malachi 2:4-5 speaks of God's covenant with Levi as "life and peace", and Isaiah 54:10 and Ezekiel 34:25 use the same phrase for God's lasting commitment to his people. Verse 13 says what this covenant holds.

decisions.choice: say: announce it; I am giving: the grant takes effect as it is spoken
decisions.reason: Moses is told to make the words known; no hearer is named. "Look, I am giving" is a solemn formula in which the speaker grants something by declaring it (as in 18:8, 21).

decisions.choice: I now give
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the formula of granting (m2) with "now" instead of the old word "behold". Readable says "announce" for "say" to make clear the words are to be made public.

source.text: וְהָ֤יְתָה לּוֹ֙ וּלְזַרְע֣וֹ אַחֲרָ֔יו בְּרִ֖ית כְּהֻנַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִנֵּא֙ לֵֽאלֹהָ֔יו וַיְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be for him and for his offspring after him a covenant of priesthood of perpetuity, because that he was jealous for his God and made atonement for [the] sons of Israel.

sw.L: Nalo litakuwa kwake na kwa uzao wake baada yake agano la ukuhani wa milele, kwa sababu alikuwa na wivu kwa ajili ya Mungu wake, akafanya upatanisho kwa ajili ya wana wa Israeli.'"
sw.B: Litakuwa kwake na kwa wazao wake baada yake agano la ukuhani wa kudumu milele, kwa sababu alionyesha wivu kwa ajili ya Mungu wake, akawafanyia Waisraeli upatanisho.'"

decisions.choice: a covenant of perpetual priesthood: the priesthood promised to his line for ages to come
decisions.reason: The priesthood already belonged to Aaron's family (Exodus 29:9; 40:15). This promise fixes it in the line of Phinehas. The lists of high priests in 1 Chronicles 5:30-41 and Ezra 7:1-5 trace the line through him. "Perpetual" means lasting, with no end in view.

decisions.choice: made atonement: dealt with Israel's guilt so that God's anger was turned away
decisions.reason: No sacrifice is offered here. By putting an end to the open sin, Phinehas removed what had brought God's anger on the people, so the plague stopped (verses 8, 11). Atonement in the law also covers turning away wrath (8:19; 17:11-12).

decisions.choice: his God: the LORD speaks of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: The LORD is speaking, but the reason is given as Moses would announce it: Phinehas was jealous "for his God". "His" refers to Phinehas.

decisions.choice: In this covenant I promise that ... will be priests
alternatives: it will be for him ... a covenant of priesthood
decisions.reason: Readable states what the covenant promises in plain words. Balanced and Readable say "zealous" and "zeal", as in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of [the] man of Israel, the struck-down one who was struck down with the Midianite [woman], [was] Zimri son of Salu, leader of a house of a father of the Simeonite[s].

en.L: And the name of the man of Israel who was struck down, who was struck down with the Midianite [woman], [was] Zimri son of Salu, leader of a father's house of the Simeonites.
en.B: The Israelite man killed along with the Midianite woman was named Zimri son of Salu; he was a leader of an ancestral family of the Simeonites.
en.R: Zimri son of Salu was the Israelite man killed with the Midianite woman. He led one of the families in the tribe of Simeon.

es.L: Y el nombre del hombre de Israel herido, que fue herido con la madianita, [era] Zimri hijo de Salu, jefe de una casa paterna de los simeonitas.
es.B: El israelita que murió junto con la madianita se llamaba Zimri hijo de Salu; era jefe de una familia patriarcal de los simeonitas.
es.R: Zimri hijo de Salu fue el israelita que murió con la madianita. Era jefe de una de las familias de la tribu de Simeón.

fr.L: Et le nom de l’homme d’Israël frappé, qui fut frappé avec la Madianite, [était] Zimri, fils de Salou, chef d’une maison paternelle des Siméonites.
fr.B: L’Israélite tué avec la Madianite s’appelait Zimri, fils de Salou ; il était chef d’une famille des Siméonites.
fr.R: Zimri, fils de Salou, était l’Israélite tué avec la Madianite. Il dirigeait une des familles de la tribu de Siméon.

sw.L: Na jina la yule mtu wa Israeli aliyepigwa, aliyepigwa pamoja na yule [mwanamke] Mmidiani, [lilikuwa] Zimri mwana wa Salu, kiongozi wa nyumba ya baba ya Wasimeoni.
sw.B: Jina la yule Mwisraeli aliyeuawa pamoja na yule mwanamke Mmidiani lilikuwa Zimri mwana wa Salu; alikuwa kiongozi wa jamaa moja ya Wasimeoni.
sw.R: Zimri mwana wa Salu ndiye aliyekuwa yule Mwisraeli aliyeuawa pamoja na yule mwanamke Mmidiani. Aliongoza mojawapo ya jamaa katika kabila la Simeoni.

decisions.choice: leader of a father's house: head of one of the family groups within the tribe of Simeon
decisions.reason: A "father's house" was an extended family within a clan and tribe (1:2). Zimri was not an ordinary man but one of the leaders of his tribe, which makes his act more serious. Simeon's numbers fall sharply between the two counts of the tribes (1:23; 26:14), though the text does not link this to Zimri.

decisions.choice: who was killed with
alternatives: who was struck down, who was struck down with
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "struck down" twice for emphasis. Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, as "killed".

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of the woman, the struck-down one, the Midianite, [was] Cozbi daughter of Zur; head of clans of a house of a father in Midian he [was].

en.L: And the name of the Midianite woman who was struck down [was] Cozbi daughter of Zur; he [was] head of the clans of a father's house in Midian.
en.B: The Midianite woman who was killed was called Cozbi daughter of Zur. Zur was head of the clans of an ancestral family in Midian.
en.R: The Midianite woman who died was Cozbi. Her father Zur was a chief who ruled over a group of family clans in Midian.

es.L: Y el nombre de la mujer herida, la madianita, [era] Cozbi hija de Zur; él [era] cabeza de los pueblos de una casa paterna en Madián.
es.B: La madianita que murió se llamaba Cozbi hija de Zur. Zur era jefe de los clanes de una familia patriarcal de Madián.
es.R: La madianita que murió era Cozbi. Su padre Zur era un jefe que gobernaba sobre un grupo de clanes familiares en Madián.

fr.L: Et le nom de la femme frappée, la Madianite, [était] Cozbi, fille de Tsour ; il [était] chef des peuplades d’une maison paternelle en Madian.
fr.B: La Madianite qui fut tuée s’appelait Cozbi, fille de Tsour. Tsour était chef des clans d’une famille de Madian.
fr.R: La Madianite qui est morte s’appelait Cozbi. Son père Tsour était un chef qui gouvernait plusieurs clans familiaux en Madian.

sw.L: Na jina la yule mwanamke aliyepigwa, yule Mmidiani, [lilikuwa] Kozbi binti Suri; yeye [alikuwa] mkuu wa koo za nyumba ya baba katika Midiani.
sw.B: Yule mwanamke Mmidiani aliyeuawa aliitwa Kozbi binti Suri. Suri alikuwa mkuu wa koo za jamaa moja katika Midiani.
sw.R: Yule mwanamke Mmidiani aliyekufa alikuwa Kozbi. Baba yake Suri alikuwa mkuu aliyetawala kikundi cha koo za jamaa katika Midiani.

decisions.choice: clans: tribal groups of people
decisions.reason: This rare word for a group of people is used of the tribes descended from Ishmael (Genesis 25:16) and of the nations (Psalm 117:1). Here it names the clans of one Midianite family group, which Zur led.

decisions.choice: Cozbi daughter of Zur: a woman of a ruling Midianite family
decisions.reason: Zur is later named among the five kings of Midian killed in the war against Midian (31:8; Joshua 13:21), and verse 18 calls Cozbi the daughter of a leader of Midian. Like Zimri, she belonged to a leading family; the affair was not a private matter between two ordinary people.

decisions.choice: Zur was head ... / Her father Zur was a chief
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ends with "he", meaning Zur. Balanced and Readable name him so that the clause is not read as being about Cozbi.

records.literal_gloss: Treat as enemies the Midianites and you will strike them.

en.L: "Treat the Midianites as enemies, and strike them.
en.B: "Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them down.
en.R: "Act as enemies toward the Midianites, and attack them.

es.L: «{{plural_you:Traten|Tratad}} a los madianitas como enemigos, y {{plural_you:hiéranlos|heridlos}}.
es.R: «{{plural_you:Pórtense|Portaos}} como enemigos de los madianitas, y {{plural_you:atáquenlos|atacadlos}}.

fr.L: « Traitez les Madianites en ennemis, et frappez-les.
fr.B: « Soyez hostiles aux Madianites et abattez-les.
fr.R: « Comportez-vous en ennemis envers les Madianites, et attaquez-les.

decisions.choice: a command to Moses that all Israel is to carry out
decisions.reason: The first verb is an unmarked form that here works as a command; the second is addressed to "you" in the plural. The order is given to Moses for the whole people, and chapter 31 tells how it was carried out (31:1-12).

decisions.choice: treat as enemies: be hostile to, as they were hostile to you
decisions.reason: The verb means to show hostility, to act as an enemy. Verse 18 uses the same verb of what the Midianites did to Israel, so the command answers like with like.

source.text: כִּ֣י צֹרְרִ֥ים הֵם֙ לָכֶ֔ם בְּנִכְלֵיהֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־נִכְּל֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם עַל־דְּבַר־פְּע֑וֹר וְעַל־דְּבַ֞ר כָּזְבִּ֨י בַת־נְשִׂ֤יא מִדְיָן֙ אֲחֹתָ֔ם הַמֻּכָּ֥ה בְיוֹם־הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה עַל־דְּבַר־פְּעֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: For hostile [are] they to you with their deceptions which they deceived you on [the] matter of Peor and on [the] matter of Cozbi daughter of [the] leader of Midian, their sister, the struck-down one on [the] day of the plague on [the] matter of Peor.

en.L: For they [are] hostile to you with their tricks with which they tricked you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of the matter of Peor."
en.B: For they are hostile to you with the tricks they played on you in the affair of Peor and in the affair of Cozbi, their kinswoman, the daughter of a leader of Midian, who was killed on the day of the plague that came because of Peor."
en.R: They are your enemies, and they have used tricks against you. They tricked you into worshiping the god of Peor, and they tricked you through Cozbi too. She was one of their own people, a Midianite leader's daughter. She died on the day the plague struck because of the sin at Peor."

es.L: Porque hostiles [son] ellos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con sus ardides con que {{plural_you:los|os}} engañaron en el asunto de Peor y en el asunto de Cozbi, hija del jefe de Madián, hermana de ellos, la que fue herida el día de la plaga por el asunto de Peor.»
es.B: Porque ellos son hostiles con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por las artimañas con que {{plural_you:los|os}} engañaron en el asunto de Peor y en el asunto de Cozbi, pariente de ellos, hija de un jefe de Madián, que fue muerta el día de la plaga que vino por causa de Peor.»
es.R: Ellos son enemigos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y han usado engaños contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} engañaron para que {{plural_you:adoraran|adorarais}} al dios de Peor, y también {{plural_you:los|os}} engañaron por medio de Cozbi. Ella era de su propio pueblo, hija de un jefe madianita. Murió el día en que la plaga azotó por causa del pecado de Peor.»

fr.L: Car ils vous [sont] hostiles par leurs ruses dont ils vous ont trompés dans l’affaire de Peor et dans l’affaire de Cozbi, fille du chef de Madian, leur sœur, qui fut frappée au jour du fléau à cause de l’affaire de Peor. »
fr.B: Car ils sont hostiles envers vous par les ruses qu’ils ont employées contre vous dans l’affaire de Peor et dans l’affaire de Cozbi, leur parente, la fille d’un chef de Madian, qui fut tuée le jour du fléau venu à cause de Peor. »
fr.R: Ils sont vos ennemis, et ils ont usé de ruses contre vous. Ils vous ont trompés pour vous faire adorer le dieu de Peor, et ils vous ont aussi trompés par Cozbi. Elle était de leur propre peuple, la fille d’un chef madianite. Elle est morte le jour où le fléau a frappé à cause du péché commis à Peor. »

sw.L: Kwa maana wao [ni] maadui kwenu kwa hila zao walizowadanganya nazo katika jambo la Peori, na katika jambo la Kozbi, binti wa kiongozi wa Midiani, dada yao, aliyepigwa siku ya pigo kwa sababu ya jambo la Peori."
sw.B: Kwa maana wanawafanyia uadui kwa hila walizowafanyia katika habari ya Peori na katika habari ya Kozbi, ndugu yao wa kike, binti wa kiongozi wa Midiani, aliyeuawa siku ya pigo lililokuja kwa sababu ya Peori."
sw.R: Wao ni maadui zenu, na wametumia hila dhidi yenu. Waliwadanganya mkamwabudu mungu wa Peori, na tena waliwadanganya kupitia Kozbi. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa watu wao, binti wa kiongozi wa Kimidiani. Alikufa siku ile pigo lilipopiga kwa sababu ya dhambi ya Peori."

decisions.choice: their tricks which they tricked you: a planned scheme to lead Israel astray
decisions.reason: The noun and verb come from one root meaning to plot or act with cunning (Genesis 37:18; Psalm 105:25). The sin at Peor is presented as a deliberate plan of the Midianites; 31:16 says it followed the advice of Balaam.

decisions.choice: the matter of Peor: the whole affair of Baal of Peor
decisions.reason: "The matter of Peor" is a short name for what happened there: the worship of Baal of Peor and the sin that went with it (verses 1-3; 31:16; Joshua 22:17).

decisions.choice: their sister: their kinswoman, one of their own people
decisions.reason: "Sister" here means a woman of the same people, as "brothers" can mean fellow tribesmen (verse 6). Cozbi's death is named because she was a Midianite of high rank (verse 15).

decisions.choice: they are hostile: an ongoing threat
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, describing what the Midianites are doing and go on doing, not only a past event.

decisions.choice: tricked you into worshiping the god of Peor
alternatives: tricked you in the matter of Peor
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the matter of Peor" was (m2) and breaks the long sentence into several.

records.literal_gloss: And it was after the plague,

en.L: And it was after the plague,

es.L: Y sucedió después de la plaga,

fr.L: Et il arriva, après le fléau,

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 25:19 is the start of 26:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. The Hebrew text counts these words as the last verse of chapter 25, while many Bibles make them the opening words of 26:1. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 26:1
decisions.reason: "And it was after the plague" introduces what follows: after the plague the LORD told Moses and Eleazar to count the people again (26:1-2). The Hebrew text ends the verse and the chapter here, so the record stops with an open sentence that continues in the next chapter. The new count comes after the old generation has died out (26:64-65).
